subject: Portability impact on SLA & feature bundling — MediWise
messages:
From: Sarah Jones <sarah.jones@mediwise.com>
To: priyom_das@redwood.example.com, kimberly_park@redwood.example.com
Date: Tue, 29 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Questions on packaging: downgrade impact & bundling

Hi Priyom / Kimberly,

Thanks again for the demo last week — Tom and I reviewed with the product team and we have a couple of follow-ups before we pull procurement in. High-level: MediWise is evaluating a move from Dedicated pools to a hosted + burst model to save unit costs, but we’re concerned about functional and SLA changes. The doc with our feature needs is attached.

Primary questions: 
- If we downgrade from Dedicated to Hosted, which features are not available (e.g., custom routing, A/B routing, per-route tracing)?
- How does the SLA change (latency percentiles, uptime, credits)?
- For bundling: can we keep the same feature set in a hosted plan by buying feature add-ons, or do some features require Dedicated by design?
- What are typical discount ranges for 12 vs 24 month commitments if we want to keep some dedicated capacity for peak windows?

Could you send a short note or table that maps Dedicated vs Hosted for the features above and the SLA delta? If helpful we can do a quick call — Tom is on PT morning schedule.

Thanks,
Sarah Jones
Head of Product Operations, MediWise
sarah.jones@mediwise.com
+1 415 555 0199

Attachment: MediWise_feature_needs_v1.pdf

From: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.example.com>
To: Sarah Jones <sarah.jones@mediwise.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.example.com>
Date: Tue, 29 Sep 2026 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Questions on packaging: downgrade impact & bundling

Hi Sarah — thanks for the clear note and the feature doc. Short answer up front: many features can be packaged on Hosted with add-ons, but there are a few Dedicated-only capabilities and the SLA/credit model does change. I pulled together an internal mapping and will attach a concise table (short version below). Can we do a 30-min sync tomorrow 9:30am PT to walk through trade-offs?

Short mapping (high level):
- Custom routing / VPC-only network controls: Dedicated-only (Hosted supports basic region routing).
- Per-route tracing and token-level cost breakdown: Hosted add-on available (slight delay in retention).
- A/B routing & canary rollouts: Hosted supports via our control plane; for high-throughput deterministic routing Dedicated recommended.
- SLA: Dedicated (99.9% uptime, 50ms p95 target on configured pool); Hosted (99.5% uptime, 80–120ms p95 typical) — formal credit table attached.

I’ll loop in Ben from pricing to propose a 12/24 month concession structure and a pilot plan for burst capacity.

Best,
Priyom
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
priyom_das@redwood.example.com

Subject: INTERNAL: MediWise — packaging / SLA questions (need numbers)

Team — quick summary from Sarah (MediWise): they want to reduce unit cost by shifting more to Hosted while keeping feature parity for observability and routing. They asked for:

1) Feature availability matrix: which features are Dedicated-only vs Hosted+addon.
2) SLA delta and credit math (what we owe at 99.5 vs 99.9).
3) Discount bands for 12/24 month deals where they keep a small Dedicated pool for peaks (they expect 30–40% baseline on Hosted, spikes to Dedicated for 2–4 hours/day).

Ask: Ben — can you draft a simple pricing sketch (monthly committed charges for small Dedicated pool + Hosted consumption) and a recommended concession (percent off list for 12 vs 24 months)? Also include whether features like A/B routing or per-route tracing require a Dedicated license or can be delivered via add-on.

I attached the customer feature doc for context. I will propose a 30-min review call with Sarah tomorrow.

Thanks,
Priyom

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.example.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.example.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.example.com>
Date: Tue, 29 Sep 2026 13:15:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: INTERNAL: MediWise — packaging / SLA questions (need numbers)

Priyom / Kim — output below (high level pricing sketch + SLA notes). I also attached a spreadsheet with the SLA-credit scenarios.

Pricing sketch (monthly, USD):
- Small Dedicated pool (2 x A100 equivalent reserved): $18,500/mo commit (predictable throughput for peak windows)
- Hosted baseline (metered): $0.0016 per token for generation (approx) — expected monthly baseline $12k–$18k depending on usage
- Add-ons (per feature, optional): per-route tracing retention $1,200/mo; A/B routing feature flag: $1,000/mo; Advanced routing (geo+latency aware): $1,500/mo

Discount guidance:
- 12-month commitment: 7–12% off committed Dedicated pool price (depending on committed volume + referenceability)
- 24-month commitment: 12–18% off (higher discounts if prepay annual)
- One-time onboarding credit: we can offer 10% onboarding credit if they commit to 12 months and include a short pilot clause.

SLA notes:
- Dedicated: 99.9% uptime target for the reserved pool; credits start at 99.6% window. Typical p95 latency guarantee is applied per-pool.
- Hosted: 99.5% uptime across shared instances; latency p95 varies by region and load (we estimate 80–120ms for their expected token lengths). Credits are lower on Hosted (formula in attached).

Recommendation: propose a hybrid pilot: 3-month pilot with small Dedicated pool + Hosted baseline, 12-month contract with a 10% onboarding credit and the option to re-evaluate the Dedicated sizing at 90 days. This protects both cost and availability.

Let me know if you want me on the call to walk pricing.

-Ben

Attachment: SLA-downgrade-impact-table.xlsx

From: Sarah Jones <sarah.jones@mediwise.com>

Subject: Re: Portability impact on SLA & feature bundling — MediWise

Thanks — this is helpful. Two clarifications before the call: 

1) Fallback behavior: if we move traffic to Hosted by default and suddenly exceed the Dedicated pool during a peak event, what is the automated fallback behavior? Do requests queue, spill to another region, or degrade to a lower-qos model? We need predictable behavior for patient-facing flows.

2) Feature bundling: is A/B routing implemented at the control plane level (so available on Hosted) or does it require Dedicated because of deterministic routing and affinity? We still need the ability to run experiments without impacting SLA for primary flows.

3) Pilot length: you suggest 3 months — can we request a 45-day pilot instead (faster procurement turnaround). Would the onboarding credit still apply?

Appreciate the attachments — we’ll review. Can you confirm the answers above in writing so procurement can attach to the purchase order?

—Sarah

Hi Sarah / Tom — quick answers and proposed next steps below. I’ll add Ben to the review call to go through pricing and the SLA spreadsheet.

Answers: 
1) Fallback behavior: we recommend a deterministic spill strategy for patient-facing flows: overflow traffic is routed to Hosted with model-variant fallback (lower-cost/quantized variant) not queued. We can configure per-route rules: (a) immediate spill to Hosted with model variant X; (b) queue up to N seconds (not recommended for patient flows); or (c) failover to region B where Dedicated capacity exists. We will document the exact routing policy in the runbook attached to the SOW.

2) A/B routing: implemented in the control plane and available in Hosted as an add-on. The difference is that Dedicated offers stronger affinity guarantees (no cross-tenant interference) — for experiments that must not impact p95 for live traffic, we recommend the hybrid approach: keep the control plane routing on Hosted and run the experiment traffic through a small Dedicated pool.

3) Pilot length & credits: we can accommodate a 45-day pilot. Onboarding credit: to qualify for the 10% onboarding credit we need a signed 12-month master subscription within 14 days of pilot completion. If procurement needs a different cadence we can carve an exception but it requires approval from RevOps.

Next steps / action items: 
- Priyom: schedule 30-min technical + commercial review tomorrow 9:30am PT (I’ll invite Ben).
- Ben: prepare the 12-month and 24-month commitment line items and attach SLA spreadsheet to the HubSpot deal.
- Sarah: confirm 9:30am PT and whether MediWise legal wants the pilot SOW (I’ll draft the SOW and attach).

Links & attachments included: HubSpot deal, Drive feature doc, DocuSign preview + SLA spreadsheet.

Thanks — looking forward to the call.

Best,
Priyom
